properties.name: Gakkel Ridge
properties.note: The slowest spreading ridge on Earth, under the Arctic ice, and the northern end of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge's line.

properties.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
properties.note: The Atlantic's spreading ridge, where the Americas move away from Europe and Africa, about as fast as fingernails grow. Iceland sits on top of it.
facts: Iceland, the Azores, Ascension, St Helena and Tristan da Cunha

properties.name: East Pacific Rise
properties.note: One of the fastest spreading ridges, where the Pacific plate moves away from the Nazca and Cocos plates. Black smokers were first found here in 1979.

properties.name: Pacific–Antarctic Ridge
properties.note: The ridge between the Pacific and Antarctic plates, in the far South Pacific.

properties.name: Chile Rise
properties.note: A spreading ridge that meets the Peru–Chile Trench off southern Chile: a ridge being swallowed by a trench.

properties.name: Galápagos Rift
properties.note: The ridge between the Cocos and Nazca plates. Deep-sea hot springs teeming with life were discovered here in 1977.

properties.name: Juan de Fuca Ridge
properties.note: A spreading ridge off the Pacific Northwest, making the Juan de Fuca plate that sinks under North America.

properties.name: Carlsberg Ridge
properties.note: The northern part of the Indian Ocean's central ridge, between India and Somalia.

properties.name: Central Indian Ridge
properties.note: The Indian Ocean's central spreading ridge, running south to the Rodrigues Triple Junction.

properties.name: Southwest Indian Ridge
properties.note: One of the slowest spreading ridges, between Africa and Antarctica.

properties.name: Southeast Indian Ridge
properties.note: The ridge between Australia and Antarctica, which split about 85 million years ago.

properties.name: Gulf of Aden Ridge
properties.note: A young ridge opening the Gulf of Aden between Arabia and Somalia.

properties.name: Red Sea Rift
properties.note: Arabia is pulling away from Africa here, about 1 cm a year: an ocean being born.

properties.name: East African Rift
properties.note: Africa is splitting in two here, Somalia from Nubia, at a few millimetres a year. Its valleys hold deep lakes and volcanoes.
facts: The Great Rift Valley; many early human fossils

properties.name: East Scotia Ridge
properties.note: A small spreading ridge behind the South Sandwich Islands.

properties.name: Mariana Trench
properties.note: The deepest place on Earth: Challenger Deep, about 10,935 m down, deeper than Everest is tall. The Pacific plate dives under the Mariana plate here.

properties.name: Izu–Ogasawara Trench
properties.note: Where the Pacific plate dives under the Philippine Sea plate, south of Tokyo.

properties.name: Japan Trench
properties.note: Off north-east Japan. The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake (magnitude 9.0–9.1) and its tsunami happened here.

properties.name: Kuril–Kamchatka Trench
properties.note: Off the Kuril Islands and Kamchatka. The 1952 Kamchatka earthquake (magnitude 9.0) happened here.

properties.name: Aleutian Trench
properties.note: Along the Aleutian Islands and southern Alaska. The 1964 Alaska earthquake (magnitude 9.2) happened here.

properties.name: Cascadia subduction zone
properties.note: The Juan de Fuca plate sinks under North America here. Its last great earthquake, about magnitude 9, was in January 1700.

properties.name: Middle America Trench
properties.note: Where the Cocos plate dives under Mexico and Central America, feeding the volcanoes of Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua.

properties.name: Peru–Chile Trench
properties.note: Also called the Atacama Trench, about 5,900 km long. The Nazca plate dives under South America, raising the Andes. The 1960 Valdivia earthquake (magnitude 9.5), the strongest ever recorded, happened here.

properties.name: Tonga Trench
properties.note: The second-deepest trench (Horizon Deep, about 10,800 m), and the fastest-moving plate boundary: about 24 cm a year near its northern end.

properties.name: Hikurangi Trough
properties.note: Off the east of New Zealand's North Island, where the Pacific plate begins to sink under the Australian plate.

properties.name: Kermadec Trench
properties.note: Running north from New Zealand to Tonga; one of the five trenches deeper than 10,000 m.

properties.name: New Hebrides Trench
properties.note: Where the Australian plate dives under Vanuatu, unusually from the west.

properties.name: Sunda Trench
properties.note: Also called the Java Trench, along Sumatra, Java and the islands to the east. The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake (magnitude 9.1–9.3) and tsunami began here.

properties.name: Philippine Trench
properties.note: East of the Philippines; the Galathea Depth, about 10,540 m, is one of the deepest points in the ocean.

properties.name: Manila Trench
properties.note: West of Luzon, where the South China Sea's floor dives under the Philippines.

properties.name: Ryukyu Trench
properties.note: Along the Ryukyu Islands, from Taiwan to Kyushu.

properties.name: Lesser Antilles and Puerto Rico Trench
properties.note: The Atlantic's deepest place, the Milwaukee Deep (about 8,376 m), is in the Puerto Rico Trench. The ocean floor dives under the Caribbean plate, making the volcanic islands of the Lesser Antilles.

properties.name: South Sandwich Trench
properties.note: East of the South Sandwich Islands; the deepest trench in the Southern Ocean.

properties.name: Hellenic Arc
properties.note: Africa sinks under the Aegean here, south of Crete, making the volcanoes of Santorini and the other Aegean islands.

properties.name: Makran subduction zone
properties.note: Off the coasts of Iran and Pakistan, where the Arabian plate sinks under Eurasia.

properties.name: Himalayan collision zone
properties.note: India has been crashing into Asia for about 50 million years, raising the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau. Everest still rises a few millimetres a year.

properties.name: Zagros collision zone
properties.note: Arabia pushing into Asia raises Iran's Zagros Mountains.

properties.name: San Andreas Fault
properties.note: California's famous fault, where the Pacific plate slides north-west past North America about 3–5 cm a year. The 1906 San Francisco earthquake happened on it.

properties.name: Queen Charlotte Fault
properties.note: The northern twin of the San Andreas Fault, off British Columbia and Alaska.

properties.name: Alpine Fault
properties.note: Along New Zealand's Southern Alps, which it is pushing up. It last broke in a great earthquake around 1717.

properties.name: North Anatolian Fault
properties.note: Turkey (the Anatolian plate) slides west past Eurasia here. The 1999 İzmit earthquake happened on it.

properties.name: Dead Sea Transform
properties.note: From the Red Sea to Turkey; the Dead Sea lies in a basin pulled open along it.
